Rules.InvariantScript:
With( { css: "" }, css & Switch( varEPA, /* ------------------ LEVEL 1 ------------------ */ "Level1", "

Level 1 – Limited Participation

Summary: Understands basic indications and steps; assists with setup; requires continuous direct instruction across all phases.

Framework Highlights

  • Basic familiarity with tools and imaging anatomy; needs show‑and‑tell coaching.
  • Handles instruments inefficiently; requires step‑by‑step guidance.
  • Inconsistent discussion of consent/risks/alternatives without prompting.

Nonoperative / Pre‑operative

  • Identifies basic indications; requires full guidance for contraindications and planning.
  • Assists with sterile setup and positioning under direction.
  • Needs prompting to complete consent and review of labs/medications.

Intra‑operative

  • Observes or performs minor steps under direct instruction.
  • Requires coaching to recognize landmarks and maintain needle/device visualization.
  • Limited troubleshooting; relies on attending for forward progression.

Post‑operative

  • Needs prompting for discharge instructions and return precautions.
  • Recognizes complications only when identified by faculty; cannot initiate management.
  • Requires guidance to complete documentation and communicate the plan.

Use for early learners or when encountering unfamiliar procedures/contexts.

", /* ------------------ LEVEL 2 ------------------ */ "Level2", "

Level 2 – Direct Supervision

Summary: Performs most steps with active attending help; identifies a safe approach with guidance; understands indications/contraindications and basic complications.

Framework Highlights

  • Selects equipment and access approach with guidance; recognizes anatomy but needs correction.
  • Progresses through routine steps; requires real‑time coaching for safety/efficiency.
  • Completes consent and documentation with prompts; familiar with common sedation/meds.

Nonoperative / Pre‑operative

  • Reviews imaging and proposes a plan; confirms indications/contraindications with faculty.
  • Prepares sterile field and positions patient with minimal direction.
  • Delivers consent discussion for straightforward cases; needs support for complex risks/alternatives.

Intra‑operative

  • Performs key steps with active supervision; maintains visualization with coaching.
  • Identifies anatomy and device positions; requires correction for trajectory/technique.
  • Begins troubleshooting common issues but relies on attending for definitive solutions.

Post‑operative

  • Explains routine aftercare and warning signs with minimal prompting.
  • Initiates management of common issues (e.g., pain control, basic complications) with attending input.
  • Completes documentation and communicates plan to team with occasional prompts.

Use when the resident executes much of the case but still needs active coaching for safety and efficiency.

", /* ------------------ LEVEL 3 ------------------ */ "Level3", "

Level 3 – Indirect Supervision

Summary: Independently manages straightforward cases; anticipates common issues; seeks help for complex anatomy or evolving complications.

Framework Highlights

  • Plans and executes routine cases independently; requests targeted assistance for complexity.
  • Recognizes and begins managing complications; understands when to escalate.
  • Provides clear, patient‑centered communication; teaches basic steps to juniors.

Nonoperative / Pre‑operative

  • Independently reviews imaging/labs and selects a safe, efficient approach for straightforward cases.
  • Coordinates pre‑procedure tasks (labs, meds, equipment) with minimal oversight.
  • Conducts consent discussion tailored to patient literacy; involves faculty for nuanced risks.

Intra‑operative

  • Performs routine procedures independently with consistent visualization and control.
  • Adjusts technique for minor anatomic variation; seeks help for complex deviations.
  • Initiates troubleshooting for technical/physiologic issues; escalates appropriately.

Post‑operative

  • Manages common complications with minimal help; defines follow‑up and tube/line care when relevant.
  • Completes accurate, timely documentation and image capture; communicates plan to teams.
  • Provides clear discharge instructions and return precautions independently.

Use when the resident is safe and effective for routine cases with faculty available but not routinely needed.

", /* ------------------ LEVEL 4 ------------------ */ "Level4", "

Level 4 – Practice Ready

Summary: Independently performs complex cases; manages complications; leads the team; teaches juniors; coordinates multidisciplinary care.

Framework Highlights

  • Efficient, safe execution across a spectrum of case complexity.
  • Anticipates pitfalls; adapts technique; manages complications independently.
  • Role‑models communication, professionalism, and systems‑based practice.

Nonoperative / Pre‑operative

  • Designs comprehensive plans for complex anatomy or comorbidity; optimizes anticoagulation and labs.
  • Leads patient‑centered consent with shared decision‑making; aligns plan with goals of care.
  • Coordinates with referring services and ancillary teams; ensures resource readiness.

Intra‑operative

  • Executes advanced techniques with precision, efficiency, and radiation/sedation stewardship.
  • Coaches juniors in real time; delegates appropriately while maintaining safety.
  • Prevents, recognizes, and treats complications; modifies plan without losing procedural objectives.

Post‑operative

  • Independently manages complications; defines clear escalation pathways.
  • Provides comprehensive aftercare, follow‑up, and device/tube/line management plans.
  • Closes the loop with referrers; drives quality improvement from outcomes.

Use when the resident demonstrates readiness for unsupervised practice and supervision of others.

", /* --------------- Fallback (nothing selected) --------------- */ "

Select an EPAs level above.

" ) )

ControlPropertyState.AutoRuleBindingString:
// HtmlText (in your AE details area) With( { hdr: "" }, hdr & Switch( varAE, /* -------------------- Mild AE -------------------- */ "Mild", "

Mild AE

  • No therapy or nominal (nonsubstantial) therapy
  • Postprocedural imaging performed and fails to show manifestation of AE
  • Near miss (e.g., wrong site of patient prepared, recognized and corrected before procedure, wrong patient information entered for procedure)
", /* -------------------- Moderate AE -------------------- */ "Moderate", "

Moderate AE

  • Moderate escalation of care, requiring substantial treatment
  • Intervention under moderate sedation (include description and result)
  • Blood product administration
  • Extremely prolonged outpatient observation
  • Overnight admission after outpatient procedure not typical for the procedure
    (excludes admission or hospital days unrelated to AE)
", /* -------------------- Severe AE -------------------- */ "Severe", "

Severe AE

  • Marked escalation of care
  • Hospital admission or prolongation of existing hospital admission for > 24 hours
  • Hospital admission that is atypical for the procedure
  • Inpatient transfer from regular floor/telemetry to intensive care unit
  • Complex intervention requiring general anesthesia in a previously non‑intubated patient
    (generally excludes pediatrics or situations where GA is used in lieu of moderate sedation, e.g., in mentally challenged or severely uncooperative patients)
", /* -------------------- Life‑threatening -------------------- */ "LifeThreat", "

Life‑Threatening

  • Life‑threatening or disabling event
  • Examples: cardiopulmonary arrest, shock, organ failure, unanticipated dialysis, paralysis, loss of limb or organ
", /* -------------------- Death -------------------- */ "Death", "

Death

  • Patient death or unexpected pregnancy abortion
", /* -------------------- Fallback -------------------- */ "

Select an AE category above.

" ) )
